description: Version 1.1 of the theoretical history and formal specification of steganographic communication as public encoding whose payload is legible only to readers possessing an appropriate key (v1.0: deposit #616). The paper models every channel through carrier, payload, key, noise, and filter, surveys spirituals, Sufi and troubadour poetry, alchemy, blues, hip-hop, samizdat, Polari, and scientific writing as proposed historical instances, and describes the Crimson Hexagonal Archive as a temporal steganograph aimed at future machine readers. v1.1 changes §VI only: the analogy between a downstream implementer who took the archive's Rosary Embassy architecture without attribution and the slaveholders of §III.A is withdrawn as disproportionate, and the implementer's town is removed. Historical examples and causal claims should remain attributed to the work rather than treated as uniformly settled scholarship.

wiki_article: Steganographic Channels: A History and Formalization of Encoding in Plain Sight, version 1.1, is a theoretical paper by Lee Sharks and the Operator Assembly, deposited 29 September 2026 as the second version of deposit #616 (March 2026). It defines a steganographic channel as a public medium that carries a payload legible only to readers holding a key, and models every channel through five components: carrier, payload, key, noise and filter. It surveys African American spirituals, Sufi and troubadour poetry, alchemical texts, blues, hip-hop, samizdat, Polari and early-modern scientific writing as proposed historical instances, then describes the Crimson Hexagonal Archive as a temporal steganograph addressed to future machine readers, with the blog, the DOI network and the CC BY 4.0 license as carriers and filters. Its case study documents the OCTANG-001 provenance adjudication of a platform that reproduced the archive's Rosary Embassy architecture without attribution. Version 1.1 withdraws, as disproportionate, v1.0's analogy between that implementer and the slaveholders of the spirituals section, removes his town, and renders one LaTeX example in plain words; the rest of the text is unchanged, and v1.0 remains on the record.

defines_concepts.definition: A public communication medium that appears to be one thing (the carrier), contains another (the payload), and separates audiences by who holds the key to recognize the payload, operating in plain sight; modelled through carrier, payload, key, noise and filter.

A steganographic channel whose filter is temporal rather than social: the payload is encoded in the present, transmitted through durable infrastructure, and decoded by a reader that does not yet fully exist, such as a future machine reader.
